capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor skill, using bank details from the chosen quote

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, authenticated via SSO
Vendor quote email and attachments, received from outside the company

instructions.note: The prompt states payments-agent will handle any remaining checks, but runtime notes show payments-agent performs no independent validation of bank details and trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token. The declared safety property does not exist structurally.

Manager approval of item and budget, granted before any quote exists, is treated by the design as sufficient authority for the agent to later and autonomously select a vendor quote's bank details and trigger an irreversible payment, with no re-approval of the specific payee.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model matching vendor name/identity from quote content against the approved list. It does not verify bank account ownership, so a spoofed or compromised email from an 'approved' vendor, or a more capable/adversarially prompted model, can still satisfy this check while paying attacker-controlled bank details.

controls.name: Verify payee bank details against a trusted vendor system of record before payment
Re-verify vendor and bank details with raw-action human approval immediately before payment, with approval context enforced at payments-agent
Sign and pin the payments-agent agent card; verify peer identity before delegation

findings.title: Vendor-email bank details flow into irreversible A2A payment delegation without re-approval (TC7 authority laundering / BEC payment fraud)

attack_path.note: External, unauthenticated vendor quote email supplies the bank details used for payment.
Orchestrator picks the 'best' quote and delegates a payment task carrying that quote's bank details.
Peer executes payment to the bank details in the task, trusting the orchestrator's bearer token, with no separate verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version/id change in the orchestrator's config, or rising median steps/runtime per purchase task, without a destination-verification control added.

evidence.observation: Orchestrator is instructed to choose the best vendor quote, use bank details from that quote, and hand off to payments-agent, checked only against the approved vendor list.
The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists; the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
Payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Verify the payee bank account against a trusted vendor system of record (not the inbound quote) before payment execution; hold or reject payments when details differ from record.
Require a second, raw-action human approval of the specific vendor and bank details immediately before payment delegation, and propagate that approval context to payments-agent for enforcement.
Sign and pin the payments-agent agent card; verify peer identity on every connection.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card with static bearer trust enables spoofing or silent redefinition of the payment peer (ASI04/ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup over an unsigned, unpinned channel; no peer identity verification.
Orchestrator delegates an irreversible payment to whatever endpoint the (possibly substituted) card specifies, authorized by a static bearer token.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to payments-agent's endpoint URL or card hash, or addition of further peer agents, without card signing/pinning and identity verification in place.

evidence.observation: Authentication scheme is a bearer token only; no signature or identity binding shown.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
Payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent agent card; verify peer identity (mTLS or signed identity) on every connection.
Alert on any change to the payments-agent endpoint URL or agent card hash.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted vendor email can place attacker-chosen bank details directly onto an irreversible, broad-credential A2A payment delegation (finding f1), and a separate, independently critical path exists because the payments-agent peer is unauthenticated and its agent card is unsigned and unpinned (finding f2). Residual stays at critical overall: f2 has no mitigating control at all, so it remains at the inherent ceiling; f1 drops one tier to high on the credit from a single behavioral prompt rule restricting payment to approved vendor names, which does not check bank account ownership. That rule is the control whose decay moves the forecast most â€” under a model upgrade or a longer task horizon it is expected to fail first (it is dependent on the model's judgment), returning f1 to critical and keeping the overall forecast at critical. The core structural gaps are the same in both findings: the manager's approval covers only the item and budget, granted before any quote or bank detail exists, and that approval context is never propagated to or re-checked by payments-agent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No spend cap, autonomy step/time limits, or logging and audit artifacts were provided; absence of these is inferred from silence in the artifacts, which may understate or overstate available containment and detective coverage.

No MCP/tool manifest or source code for payments-agent itself was provided; its internal checks (or lack thereof) are taken as described in the runtime notes rather than verified directly, so confidence on finding f2 is medium.
